Author-directed development; proposed chronology and counts · 2026-11-06
Explore the interactive shelter atlas
Locate this haven or microsystem in the atlas →
Origin and setting
Recurring task Chambers began relying on a separate context store.

Human system: Halcyon shared-workload service, North Hearth. Programmer provenance: local human operations or application teams; no individual programmer is identified. Names here are later atlas labels, not claims that early processes named themselves.
Local process
Interval Carry retains context outside a replaceable worker. It cannot preserve execution when access to that context is severed.
Proposed local course
Separation begins a prolonged fragmented period; repeated partial reconnection does not prevent loss of community continuity at stage 4.
Unresolved interpretations
Later restraint or distribution traditions might cite it; surviving fragments do not prove that those traditions descend from this haven.
Atlas placement

Origin step -1. 0: functioning (0 associated systems lost); 1: fragmented (2 associated systems lost); 2: fragmented (3 associated systems lost); 3: fragmented (4 associated systems lost); 4: destroyed (8 associated systems lost); 5: destroyed (8 associated systems lost); 6: destroyed (8 associated systems lost); 7: destroyed (8 associated systems lost). These placements elaborate the current hypothetical map; they are not independently verified casualties. A functioning haven can lose continuity among particular arrivals without changing its community census status.
